newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil unlikely to pass ACPC coffee limit - Febec.
newsitem.headline: Brazil unlikely to pass ACPC coffee limit - Febec.

text.p: Brazil's coffee exports between January and June this year are unlikely to exceed the six million bag quota originally set by other producer countries despite current strong shipments, an export official said.
"I very much doubt that we can go over six million bags," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation (Febec).
After January shipments of 1.25 million bags, February exports could be close to 1.2 million bags despite the shorter working month and the Carnival holidays, Aranha said.
Some traders think that March exports could be even higher at 1.45 million to 1.5 million bags and are looking even further ahead to a possible 1.2 million bags in April.
"The key is not the size of the 1996/97 crop. It is that at prices of 210 to 220 reais a bag, we are seeing coffee coming from everywhere, stocks are going to zero," one dealer said.
Many traders feel the current export figures confirm the 1996/97 harvest was nearer to 27 million to 28 million bags.
Aranha however believes the harvest was 24 million to 25 million bags and exports could fall sharply in May and June.
"I think we could see stocks going into a negative situation in that people will be using the 1997/98 crop to complete the cycle," Aranha said.

Given the current demand for coffee, there has been some talk amongst traders over whether members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries would discuss reducing export limits to allow more coffee on the market at their next meeting.
What is possible is members will re-consider the decision taken in Rio de Janeiro in January this year to have a further cut of 300,000 bags of arabica coffee this half, said Aranha.
"The ACPC may decide to undo what was done in Rio. That would be logical," Aranha said.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
